questions.q: Why is 'the report shows the wrong numbers' considered an especially vague ticket to start with?
options: It isn't vague — it always means the same specific thing
It always means the report tool is broken
It could stem from many different causes (currency conversion, parameter error, timing cutoff, reconciliation break, incomplete data), so the first job is to get a specific, comparable number
It can only be caused by a security issue
questions.explain: A vague 'report is wrong' complaint could map to many different underlying causes; getting a specific, comparable figure is the necessary first step before diagnosing further.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of the $340,000 difference between the Balance Sheet report and Smart View?
options: A currency conversion error
A duplicate asset was entered
An invalid account combination
The Balance Sheet report ran at 7:00 AM, before a Mass Additions batch posted at 7:45 AM; Smart View was refreshed after the batch posted
questions.explain: Both figures were accurate for the moment they were generated — the report simply ran before new equipment had posted into the active asset register, while Smart View reflected the later state.

questions.q: How is this ticket's root cause conceptually similar to Lesson 14's customer statement ticket?
options: Both involve a timing difference where data that is correct can still appear 'missing' or inconsistent depending on when a report or statement was generated relative to a cutoff
They are unrelated concepts
Both involve a duplicate invoice
Both require reversing a GL journal
questions.explain: Both tickets show the same underlying principle: a transaction or posting that is legitimately excluded or included depending on timing, not because of a data or system error.

questions.q: What was the correct resolution for this ticket?
options: Manually adjust the Balance Sheet report's total to match Smart View
Re-run the Balance Sheet report after confirming the Mass Additions batch had posted, and explain the timing difference to the controller
Reverse the Mass Additions batch
Escalate to Oracle support as a system defect
questions.explain: Since nothing was actually wrong with the data, the fix was simply re-running the report after the batch posted and explaining why the discrepancy occurred.

questions.q: According to the course recap, what common discipline ran through every ticket worked in this course?
options: Always override holds immediately to resolve tickets faster
Always assume the invoice or report itself is broken
Get specific about the symptom, isolate what's actually different, check the real evidence, confirm the theory before fixing, apply the narrowest correct fix, and document honestly
Escalate every ticket to Oracle support
questions.explain: This discipline — isolate, confirm, fix narrowly, document honestly — was the thread running through every ticket across all six chapters of the course.
